observations.observed_fact: Ken Newquist describes sketching an original homegrown region, recreating it in Hexographer, then using Worldographer. Paper, digital map and notes diverged: a tower changed side, a town separation differed, and paper/digital hex offsets did not match. He reports reconciling the maps.
observations.interpretation: Primary evidence of both map creation and concrete maintenance friction. This is not a ready-made setting import, nor proof that an automatic generator alone solves the synchronization problem.

operational_requirement.source_rule_ref: obs-DND5-SCALES-MAP-20261110 (observed GM practice, not a rule)
operational_requirement.normative_kind: non-normative problem report; optional product interpretation
operational_requirement.applicability: L1 correction and continued maintenance of a prepared regional map
operational_requirement.trigger_or_user_action: Correct a previously prepared named tower from a chosen western hex to a chosen southern hex.

inputs_and_units.object: one prepared Tower with an existing name and note
inputs_and_units.content: retain current tower description and note; no random regeneration

operational_requirement.product_operation: Relocate existing prepared content consistently and retain the accepted correction when saving/reopening or exporting that map.
operational_requirement.expected_output: One Tower at the selected southern hex with the same name and note; the former western placement no longer appears.
constraints_and_exceptions: Example is a synthetic acceptance fixture motivated by an actual location disagreement; not a mandatory DND5 rule.
No promise to detect or synchronize changes in an external paper map or bullet journal.
Do not infer coordinates/offset convention from a6-mile hex statement; those parameters remain source-specific unknowns.
Future underground layer is not a new deficiency or authorized extension of active051.
Current HexCrawl support for this exact move/persistence profile is unknown; presence of a canonical rule is not implementation evidence.

acceptance_cases.given: A named Tower with note N on selected western hex; chosen southern hex is empty and admissible
acceptance_cases.when: Accept moving the Tower to the southern hex
acceptance_cases.expected: Exactly one Tower appears on the southern hex; name and note N remain; no Tower remains on the former hex

acceptance_cases.given: The map after the accepted Tower correction
acceptance_cases.when: Save and reopen the same editable document without regeneration
acceptance_cases.expected: Tower remains at the southern hex with the same name/note; other map content and placements remain unchanged

acceptance_cases.given: The same corrected map with the Tower selected
acceptance_cases.expected: Export places Tower in the accepted southern position rather than the original western position; exporting does not move content

operational_requirement.source_vs_product_interpretation: The reports establish a reconciliation problem. The common relocation/persistence outcomes are research examples for the existing editing area; no command/API/specification, auto-import promise or new source-game binding is created.
